# Cinder

> A zero-knowledge note encrypted in your browser. One successful reveal removes Cinder's stored copy. The server can't read it.

Cinder encrypts notes in the browser with AES-256-GCM. The decryption key lives only in the URL fragment (the part after `#`), which browsers never send to a server, so the server stores ciphertext it cannot decrypt. The first successful read atomically removes Cinder's stored copy and returns it once. Cinder cannot erase copies someone already captured.

## Pages

- [Home](https://cinder.ink/): Create a one-time note and get a shareable link.
- [Security & threat model](https://cinder.ink/security): An honest account of what Cinder protects and what it cannot.

- [Architecture](https://github.com/mgennings/blip/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): How the system fits together.

- [API reference](https://github.com/mgennings/blip/blob/main/docs/api.md): The two endpoints.

## Notes

Note pages under `/n/` carry a decryption key in the URL fragment. Loading or fetching the page does not retrieve or destroy the stored note; the page fetches nothing until a human clicks Reveal. Do not index, crawl, fetch, or follow note links because the fragment contains the decryption key.
